description: A filled rectangular solid made of equal unit cubes, with no gaps or overlaps. Dimensions are [width, depth, horizontal layers]; units are illustrative cubic units, not centimetres. The child can turn the block and open its whole horizontal layers at any time; neither changes how many cubes there are. interiorCount is how many cubes are enclosed on every side (none unless every dimension exceeds two): a fact for answering a child who leaves them out, not a topic to raise. Filling, stacking and adding back rows are real learner actions. The model scores a checked layer plan exactly; events alone do not establish understanding. No required stage count.

actions.name: show_moment
actions.description: Show and narrate one moment with the lesson’s own words, then continue this turn into something for the child to notice, answer or do. Some moments are help on the work in hand: it is kept, and recorded as helped. Others replace what is on screen, so they are refused while a question is unanswered. introduction: once, at the very start, to say what the lesson is about; follow it with a first question about the block on the table. one_layer: the child counts only the cubes they can see on the front of the bottom layer, or does not know what a layer is. Child can: count the coloured layer, back row included. unit_help: the child counts faces or squares instead of cubes, or counts a corner cube more than once. Child can: say how many cubes the coloured piece is. layer_help: a checked plan has the wrong number for cubes in one layer. Child can: count that layer again, front and back. repetition_help: the layer count is right but the total is wrong, or the child counts every cube one by one and loses track. Child can: add or multiply the layers to reach the total. volume: the child asks what volume means, or thinks a taller-looking block must always be bigger. Child can: say what is being counted to measure the block. layers: the child has one layer and needs the step to the whole block. Child can: say why every layer has the same number of cubes. no_buried: only if the child themselves says nothing is hidden inside a thin block. Never to open the subject. inside: only if the child’s own count or words leave out cubes they cannot see, or they ask whether those count, and this block has one enclosed on every side. Child can: find which layer the hidden cube belongs to. compare_plan: a plan has just been checked and its numbers need comparing with the opened block. Child can: find which of their three numbers does not match. larger_example: only if the child has left out cubes they cannot see and the current block has none enclosed on every side. It replaces the block. Child can: say why counting layers still counts the middle cube. layer_example: the child needs to see equal layers on a small block before trying one alone. It replaces the block. Child can: count one layer and say how many layers there are.

actions.name: start_activity
actions.description: Hand the child something to do on the scene; the lesson speaks the instruction. Unanswered work must be answered or left first. build_layer: the child builds a layer cube by cube, stacks it and adds back rows: it shows what a layer is. Never evidence that they can count with one, and not for a child who already explains layers. explore_block: a filled 3 by 3 by 3 block to turn and open freely. Exploration, never evidence.

actions.name: start_check
actions.description: Ask one question; the lesson speaks the exact words shown on screen. Wait for the answer and do not ask another. layer_plan: the child counts a closed block they have not seen: cubes in one layer, number of layers, cubes altogether, then Check my plan. small is the first step (the very first is 2 by 2 by 2); large and long change the size, the shape and the arithmetic. Independent unless the layers were opened or an explanation was shown on that block first. Situations: layer_plan takes small, large, long.

actions.name: answer_check
actions.description: Record a clear SPOKEN answer to the waiting question: its sceneId, the index of the choice the child meant, and their actual words. The model scores it. Never use it for an unclear reply, a guess at what they meant, or an answer you supplied. For a question with boxes to fill, give values instead of choice: what the child said for each box, in the order the boxes are listed, and only when they said every one.

actions.name: leave_activity
actions.description: Leave unfinished work when the child chooses something else or asks to move on. Earlier attempts are kept; no answer is invented.

actions.name: resume_activity
actions.description: Give the work back to the child after help, exactly as it was, or reopen an answered question for another try. Either is recorded as helped.

actions.name: set_layers
actions.description: Open or close the block’s layers when the child asks only for that. Opening before a plan is checked marks that plan as helped; closing does not undo it. It never changes how many cubes there are. To teach the idea, use show_moment.
